contentBlocks.text: You've learned digraphs, where two letters make one new sound. Today: a blend, where two letters keep their OWN sounds but are said quickly together.

In a blend like 'st', you still hear both the /s/ and /t/ sounds — they're just blended together quickly, unlike a digraph where the two letters become one totally new sound. Practice reading these words with 'st': stop, stem, best, fast. Notice the difference from digraphs: in 'ch' and 'sh', you can't hear the individual letters anymore, but in 'st', you still can if you listen closely.
You now understand the real difference between a digraph (one new sound) and a blend (two sounds said quickly together)! Tomorrow we'll read two new sentences using everything from this week.

objectives: Explain the difference between a consonant blend and a digraph
Blend and read words with 'st' in starting and ending positions
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review 'sh' and 'ch' as digraphs from this week and last.
2. Introduce 'st' as a blend, explicitly contrasting it with a digraph — both sounds are still audible.
3. Blend stop, stem, best, and fast together, listening for both /s/ and /t/.
4. Move to the worksheet: read, trace, and write each word.
5. Close by saying a digraph word and a blend word back to back, noticing the difference.
differentiationTips: Struggling: don't worry about the digraph-vs-blend terminology yet — focus on successfully blending the four words
Ready for more: ask the child to sort this week's words (chip, much, stop, best) into 'digraph' and 'blend' categories
This digraph-vs-blend distinction is a genuinely important phonics concept, worth real time even if the terminology itself isn't mastered yet
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a reading, tracing, and writing activity — check that the child can blend all four 'st' words and can explain (in simple terms) that a blend keeps both sounds while a digraph makes one new sound.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Introduces consonant blends as a distinct phonics category from digraphs, broadening the decoding toolkit built through this week's short-vowel and digraph work.

generationData.instructions: Read each word by blending its sounds (remember: in a blend, you hear BOTH sounds), trace it, then write it once more on your own.
